sections.body: INTEREST is money paid for using money. Banks may pay you interest on savings, and you pay interest when you borrow.
SIMPLE interest is paid only on the original amount. 1,000 at 10% simple interest earns 100 every year.
COMPOUND interest is paid on the original amount AND on interest already earned. 1,000 at 10%: year 1 → 1,100; year 2 → 1,210; year 3 → 1,331.
Compounding helps savers grow money over time. But it also makes debts grow fast if you don't pay them off!
Rule of 72: divide 72 by the interest rate to estimate how many years it takes money to double. At 6%, about 12 years.
Use a calculator: what does 500 become after 5 years at 8% compound interest? Multiply by 1.08 five times.

quiz.q: You save 200 at 5% SIMPLE interest. How much interest do you earn in 3 years?
hints: Simple interest is the same every year.
First find 5% of 200, then think about 3 years.
Example: 100 at 10% simple → 10 a year → 3 years = 30.

quiz.q: Why does compound interest grow faster than simple interest?
options: You also earn interest on past interest
The rate goes up every year
hints: What is the interest calculated on in year 2?
With compounding, last year's interest becomes part of the amount.
quiz.explain: Each year's interest is added to the total, so the next year you earn interest on it too.

quiz.q: Using the Rule of 72, about how long does money take to double at 9% a year?
